subject.title: Session transcript doomloop: crash-restart cycle inflates transcript until gateway OOMs

question: Which default recovery policy should OpenClaw apply when an active session transcript is already oversized or poison-restarts the gateway on reload?
rationale: Source evidence supports the bug, but automation cannot choose the data-retention and UX tradeoff between default quarantine, truncation, compaction, skip-on-load, and doctor-guided recovery.

options.title: Default bounded recovery
options.body: Add a default pre-open guard that moves oversized or repeatedly crashing transcripts into an explicit degraded recovery path before whole-file repair/open, with doctor or CLI recovery guidance.

options.title: Opt-in only
options.body: Keep maxActiveTranscriptBytes as an operator opt-in and document manual recovery, accepting that default installs can still hit this crash-restart boundary.

options.title: Split narrow fixes
options.body: Land the bootstrap-marker cap separately and split media dedupe or loader streaming into focused follow-ups while this issue remains open as the umbrella.

recommendation.title: Default bounded recovery
recommendation.body: Add a default pre-open guard that moves oversized or repeatedly crashing transcripts into an explicit degraded recovery path before whole-file repair/open, with doctor or CLI recovery guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work and history place vincentkoc closest to the session repair, transcript cache, and bootstrap helper surfaces implicated by the recovery decision.
